name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a 2-pixel solid focus ring with a 1-pixel outer glow at 15% opacity.

This gives keyboard users a clear, visible target without blurring edges on high-DPI screens. The glow helps it stand out against busy backgrounds while keeping the ring sharp. Trade-off: the glow adds a slight visual weight, but it’s worth it for users who rely on focus indicators to navigate.

name: Reader
text: Tabbing through the proposed design, I flag the 2-pixel solid focus ring with a 1-pixel outer glow as it may still not provide sufficient contrast for users with low vision. A better alternative would be a 4-pixel solid focus ring, which would provide a clearer visual cue without relying on the glow. This would settle the argument if user testing confirms that the thicker ring is more easily perceived by users with visual impairments.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a 4-pixel solid focus ring with no glow. This meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for low-vision users without relying on glow, which can blur on high-DPI screens. The thicker ring gives a stronger visual cue while keeping edges sharp. Trade-off: it takes slightly more space, but that’s better than risking invisibility for some users.

name: Reader
text: A 4-pixel ring risks crowding small interactive elements—like buttons in tight toolbars—making them harder to tap on mobile or hit with a keyboard. A better fix: keep the 2-pixel ring but boost its contrast to WCAG 2.1 AA by darkening the color, not thickening it. Settle it with a contrast checker and user testing on low-vision simulators.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt a 2-pixel solid focus ring with WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (no glow) to balance clarity, space efficiency, and cross-device usability. Owner: Ramp must deliver the ring style in CSS with contrast verified via checker.
